clue.text: Difficulty stopping offensive remarks in island nation

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, so one word sits inside the other here

parts.note: barbs are cutting, hurtful remarks
ado is fuss or trouble, as in 'without further ado'

explanation.surface: Some awkwardness arises as rude comments fly around in a Caribbean country.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is an independent Caribbean country occupying a single island, so it is literally an island nation.

clue.text: When surface wiped, silver possibly remains

indicators.note: wiping the surface clears off the top layer, which in a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: silver coins are one example of money in hand

explanation.surface: Polishing tarnished silverware leaves a residue behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Lose the C at the top of CASH and ASH is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is what is left behind after burning, especially cremated human remains kept in an urn.

clue.text: Piebald sozzled, two of its legs gone?

indicators.note: sozzled means very drunk, and a drunk staggers about out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patchy-coated horse has had so much to drink it can barely stand on all fours.
explanation.walkthrough: A piebald is a horse with black and white patches; a four-legged creature with two legs gone would walk on two.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipedal describes an animal walking on two feet, which is what a four-legged beast becomes after losing a pair.

clue.text: Dictator's Canute, say? Reluctantly stoop down

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone dictating a letter, so the word is to be spoken out loud

parts.note: King Canute was a Dane, a ruler from Denmark

explanation.surface: A tyrant speaks of the old king who could not command the tide, and grudgingly bows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant beside a king; here it is simply someone speaking words for writing down.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, doing something one thinks beneath one's dignity, which is grudgingly lowering oneself.

clue.text: Mean family discontented after gin is drunk

indicators.note: after places the part named before it behind the part named after it
drunk means intoxicated and reeling, so the letters before it stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: read as dis-contented: with its contents taken out, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: the two end letters of family

explanation.surface: A stingy household is unhappy once the gin has been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' poses as stingy, describing the family, but it is the verb, and 'is' belongs to the fodder rather than the grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: To signify is to indicate or convey a sense, which is what a word does when it means something.

clue.text: See 27
Cook bit of fish? Snapper finally eaten

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the char is a fish of the trout family, and its gill is one bit of it

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of snapper

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to cook a piece of fish, adding that the snapper has been finished off.
explanation.walkthrough: Snapper looks like the fish, but only its last letter counts; put R inside CHAR GILL to get CHARGRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: To chargrill is to cook food over hot charcoal or a ridged pan, a specific method of cooking.

clue.text: Outstanding artwork finished up being broken by priest

indicators.note: a word broken by another is split open with the other placed in the gap
in a down entry up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: over means ended, as in 'the game is over'
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A splendid painting is complete but has been damaged by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise, but in sculpture it means standing out from the background.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievo, from Italian, is relief sculpture in which figures project, or stand out, from a flat background.

clue.text: Pale, top line blurred in the paper

indicators.note: something blurred loses its clear shape, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The first line of a newspaper column has come out faint and smudged.
explanation.definitionFit: En papillote is French cookery for food baked inside a parcel of paper or foil, so literally cooked in the paper.

clue.text: Conveyance that's certainly rolling around filled by grotesque one-legged creature?

indicators.note: a word filled by another has the other placed inside it
rolling around turns the word over so it reads back to front

parts.note: yes is an emphatic agreement, like 'certainly!'
a troll is an ugly creature of folklore, and with one leg it would get about by hopping

explanation.surface: A vehicle that certainly gets about is stuffed with a hideous hopping monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed word is split open to hold the creature, with its first letter staying out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping trolley is a wheeled basket for carrying goods round a supermarket, so a humble kind of conveyance.

clue.text: Since bound to be on a slant

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was raining'
a lope is a long bounding stride

explanation.surface: Something certain to end up tilted, perhaps a picture on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' suggests obliged, as in 'bound to be', but it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslope is an adverb meaning tilted or sloping, exactly the position of something lying at a slant.

clue.text: Awkward moves — to pop music?

parts.note: surface reading: clumsy steps on the dance floor while chart hits play; setter's reading: pop is a father, so this is the music of a father, and the clumsy jigging of middle-aged fathers at parties

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles clumsily on the dance floor while the latest chart songs play.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop is a colloquial word for father, so pop music is a father's kind of dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad dancing is the informal name for the embarrassing, uncoordinated way middle-aged men dance at parties and weddings.

clue.text: Where case taken from ambulance stretched out?

parts.words: Where case taken from ambulance stretched out
parts.note: surface reading: the hospital department where a patient arriving by ambulance is brought; setter's reading: the case, or outer letters, of ambulance are A and E, and A&E written out in full is the department's name

explanation.surface: A patient is lifted out of an ambulance and laid on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretched out' sounds like lying on a stretcher, but it means expanding an abbreviation to its full form.
explanation.definitionFit: Accident and emergency is the British hospital department treating urgent cases, the equivalent of an emergency room or ER.

clue.text: See something like The Sixth Sense?

parts.note: extrasensory perception is often called the sixth sense
the suffix -y turns a noun into an adjective meaning like it, as in rosy

explanation.surface: A question about seeing a film resembling the supernatural thriller The Sixth Sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sixth Sense looks like the film title; read it as ESP, and ESPY would mean ESP-like.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or spot something, a literary synonym for seeing it.

clue.text: Art of rowing, arguably, where domestic chores would get done?

definitions.text: where domestic chores would get done

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat with oars
the suffix -ery names an art or practice, as in cookery or archery

explanation.surface: Rowing is offered as an art form, a claim open to argument, in a room where housework happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arguably' admits that SCULL-ERY, the art of sculling, is a made-up word; it also nods to rowing as arguing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery is a small back kitchen where washing up and other menial household work was traditionally done.

clue.text: See 12
Pig's unlikely boast when guzzling on — chance would be a fine thing!

definitions.text: chance would be a fine thing!

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing greedily, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: 'pigs might fly' describes the impossible, so a pig saying 'I fly' is an unlikely boast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A greedy pig brags while gobbling its food, and someone scoffs at the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke rests on the saying 'pigs might fly', used to dismiss something that will never happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are wistful exclamations wishing for something one does not expect to happen, so they are interchangeable idioms.

clue.text: Ballet princess when slipping over regretted oath, to some extent

indicators.note: something slipping over turns upside down, so the letters are read backwards
to some extent means partly, so only a portion of the words is used

parts.note: the run of letters from the end of regretted into the start of oath

explanation.surface: A dancer playing royalty takes a fall and regrets a promise she made.
explanation.definitionFit: Odette is the princess turned into a swan in Tchaikovsky's ballet Swan Lake, its heroine role.

clue.text: See 9
Second chooser, one making a choice

parts.note: s is the standard abbreviation for second
an elector is a voter, one who chooses

explanation.surface: Another person chooses, and is the one deciding.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector picks things, such as players for a team, so is someone who makes the pick.

clue.text: Limit in power where boat launched

indicators.note: in places the word before it inside the word after it

parts.note: sway is influence or control, as in 'hold sway'
a lip is an edge or rim, the limit of a vessel

explanation.surface: A restriction on authority applies at the place where a ship goes into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipway is a sloping ramp running into water down which ships are launched or hauled up.

clue.text: Old player, opener for Pakistan left prodding every inch of cricket pitch

indicators.note: prodding means poking into something, so these pieces are pushed inside

parts.note: a chain is an old measure of 22 yards, exactly the length of a cricket pitch

indicators.note: an opener is the one who goes first, so take the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Pakistan
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A veteran cricketer, Pakistan's opening batsman, is left-handed and pokes about the whole of the wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' and 'opener' look like cricket, but the player is an actor; the chain is an old surveyor's measure few solvers know.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was a silent-film actor of the early twentieth century, so a performer from long ago.

clue.text: Dope with a little brain, foolish

indicators.note: a little means only a small portion is taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the end of brain run into the start of foolish

explanation.surface: An idiot who has hardly any intelligence is acting stupidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'foolish' both suggest stupidity, but dope is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is informal slang for inside information or facts, the same sense as the clipped word for information.

clue.text: Writer with page to make cryptic, solution providing some relief, early on?

definitions.text: solution providing some relief, early on

indicators.note: making something cryptic means scrambling it so it cannot be read straight

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An author fills a page with a puzzle, and the answer gives some relief at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' suggests the answer to a crossword, but it is a liquid, and 'early on' means in infancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gripe water is a liquid remedy given to babies to ease colic and wind, so it soothes infants.

clue.text: Final word of reverence before medicine at the bottom pushed up — that's that!

definitions.text: Final word of reverence before medicine at the bottom pushed up — that's that!

indicators.note: in a down entry pushing up makes the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: amen is the word closing a prayer

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter, the one at its end

parts.note: the last letter of medicine

explanation.surface: A prayer's closing word comes before a dose of something unpleasant, and the matter is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: AMEN then E, read upwards, gives ENEMA; and the whole clue also describes one: medicine at the bottom, pushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is liquid injected into the rectum, quite literally a treatment administered from behind and forced upward.

clue.text: Fish dipping both sides in sea

indicators.note: dipping in means going down into something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
right and left, R and L, are the two sides

explanation.surface: A fish plunging both flanks into the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A marlin is a large ocean game fish with a long spear-like upper jaw, a prized catch.

clue.text: Over a few days, third of milk fed to King's hairy baby?

indicators.note: something fed to a baby goes into it, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: King Kong is the giant hairy ape, so his baby would be a wee Kong, wee being Scottish for small

indicators.note: third of points to the letter in third position of the word

parts.note: the third letter of milk

explanation.surface: Over several days a large hairy infant is given a bottle of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes into WEE KONG after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeklong describes something lasting seven days, so it extends over a span of several days.

clue.text: One in order, one fewer picked up?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the sound counts

parts.note: take one away from one and you have none

explanation.surface: Someone tidying a row of items picks one up, leaving one fewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' suggests tidiness, but it is a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a woman who belongs to a religious order, living under its vows.

clue.text: Opera company, vehicle bringing delicate things to the table, for audition?

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the words are meant to be listened to

parts.words: vehicle bringing delicate things to the table
parts.note: a doily is a lacy mat set under food on a table, so a cart carrying them is a doily cart

explanation.surface: A troupe of singers is wheeled in on a trolley full of fragile tableware, ready to try out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' fits an opera company trying out singers, but here it simply means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The D'Oyly Carte Opera Company is the British troupe famous for staging the comic operas of Gilbert and Sullivan.

clue.text: In work escorting lady, ultimately — and getting the urge?

indicators.note: escorting means walking alongside, so the two pieces are placed next to each other
ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter

parts.note: the last letter of lady
someone in work is earning a wage

explanation.surface: A man employed as a companion to a woman finds himself feeling desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearning is longing or craving for something, which is the state of feeling a strong desire.
